findings.reason: The bound is a bare module constant that is not sealed into the preparation receipt or captured job. createIdentityReviewBundle in scripts/lib/people-identity-review-record.mjs recomputes the expected split with the current MAX_IDENTITY_REVIEW_TRANSPORT_BYTES and requires job.parts.length === expected.length plus byte-identical part transports. Any part job prepared or captured under the 768 KiB bound (for example the 2-part Jinshu 093 layout) therefore can no longer be recorded after adoption, and nothing detects or reports this up front; it only fails at record time with a generic 'All captured independent review parts are required'. This fails closed, but there is no migration path, pinned bound, or receipt field (such as maxBytes) to keep in-flight captured reviews reproducible.

assembleChapterIdentityReviewParts requires one actual reviewer across all parts (new Set(actualReviewerAgentIds).size === 1). Every part repeats the full target chapter units, so the real093 calibration shows total transport growing from 1,205,376 bytes (2 parts) to 2,027,385 bytes (9 parts). If that single retained reviewer processes the parts in one conversation, as this review flow does, the cumulative context grows about 68 percent. The new comment claims the change keeps review 'below the compaction-heavy size observed in Jinshu 093', but the packet only proves per-part size, not reduced reviewer compaction. The rationale is unproven, and the change may make the observed failure worse unless each part is a fresh conversation with the same agent ID.

The tests pass explicit maxBytes (4000 or 1024) and never exercise MAX_IDENTITY_REVIEW_TRANSPORT_BYTES. Nothing tests the new 256 KiB value, the single-case-exceeds-bound failure at that value, or the prepare-to-record round trip where createIdentityReviewBundle must reproduce the 9-part split. Real093's largest part is 254,432 bytes, only about 7.7 KB under the bound, so a small source or registry delta could make one case exceed it ('Identity case ... exceeds the inspected transport bound'), and no test covers this. Passing tests do not cover the changed line.

reason: Code-only review of the single-line change in scripts/lib/people-identity-review-transport.mjs (768*1024 to 256*1024), based on the complete module, both native callers (scripts/prepare-people-chapter-identity.mjs and scripts/lib/people-identity-review-record.mjs), the partition tests, the construction-compatibility receipt, and the real093 calibration in the packet. Split behaviour itself is unchanged: project() still includes every target-chapter unit, every claim and mention unit of owned people and anchors, and every candidate header, and it throws on missing evidence. Case ownership is still checked for exact, ordered, non-duplicated coverage in both split and assemble. Author exclusion and single-reviewer identity are still enforced. assertCapturedIdentityReviewParts validates already-saved receipts without recomputing the split, so retained certified proofs should still revalidate through the saved-proof path; I could not verify this because validateChapterIdentityBundle and people-chapter-identity.mjs are not in the packet. Publication paths still emit dataQualified:false and published:false. The construction graph is unchanged per the receipt. I am holding because the bound is not pinned into captured provenance, which strands in-flight 768 KiB part captures at record time, and because the stated anti-compaction benefit is contradicted by the calibration's total-bytes growth under the one-reviewer requirement. Limitations: I did not run code, I had no access to the logs referenced in localValidation, and I did not see validator internals or the actual 093 data. This is not an approval of any chapter, identity, date, or ebook.
